messages:
Aisha: Quick follow-up from the runtime-compat RFC — we need to align on the 'sentinel' contract between onboarding and runtime. Can we sketch the minimal signal set that prober + runtime should exchange?
Tom: TL;DR: health + schema-hash + kv-warmup-status + backpressure-level. keep it tiny.
Devin: Agree on small set. Also add a "golden-match" flag that indicates probe matched golden inputs during warmup. We use that for early gating.
Kai: "golden-match" seems useful but expensive to compute for large models. Could we make it optional per-model?
Aisha: Yes optional per-model. Default = off for >4B or when runtime detects long-prep.
Maya: How does this interact with backpressure? If warmup is slow we should surface a soft-fail so canary traffic routes to fallback variant.
Tom: Proposal: sentinel = { health: ok|degraded|fail, schema_hash: hex, kv_warmup: pct_complete (0-100), golden_match: pass|fail|na, backpressure: low|med|high }
Devin: Looks good. Add last_probe_ts so controller can detect stale sentinels.
Aisha: +1 last_probe_ts. Also add a version field for the sentinel format to allow rolling changes.
QA-Jen: From QA: we need a stable set of telemetry metrics emitted when sentinel transitions: warmup_started, warmup_completed, golden_mismatch, backpressure_rise. Those feed SLO alerts.
Kai: Concern: emitting all those metrics at high cardinality (model+pool+region) will cost a lot. Suggest sampling telemetry during onboarding; full telemetry only for failures.
Maya: Sampling sounds right. Can we do deterministic sampling keyed by model-id so we at least cover some models?
Tom: Implementation note: prober will post sentinel to /runtime/sentinel/<model-id> as a tiny JSON. Runtime returns 200/202. Controller polls the sentinel endpoint every 10s for active onboarding.
Aisha: If runtime reports backpressure=high for >30s, controller should: pause canary, spin up fallback variant (quantized or smaller), and notify SRE channel.
Devin: For fallback, define explicit compatibility tags so controller knows which fallback is safe (e.g., token-stream, kv-compatible). We need a small compatibility matrix in model metadata.
QA-Jen: We'll add tests that simulate partial kv_warmup and assert controller follows pause+fallback path.
Kai: Edgecase: multi-shard models — sentinel needs per-shard warmup pct. Suggest kv_warmup become list or encoded string. Simpler: make kv_warmup a two-part field: overall_pct and worst_shard_pct.
Aisha: Keep API simple: kv_warmup_overall and kv_warmup_worst_shard. Both ints 0-100.
Maya: Ops-bot: will wire alerts: if golden_mismatch -> create ticket in #eng-ml and ping model-owner. If backpressure high -> page SRE after 5 mins.
ops-bot: noted. will use @oncall escalation policy. :thumbsup:
Tom: Docs + SDK: include a tiny helper to validate sentinel schema and a CLI to fetch sentinel for debugging: `rictl sentinel get <model-id>`
Devin: Also add a debug flag to include last 3 probe logs in sentinel on demand (bounded size) so oncall can triage quickly.
Aisha: Good. Last open question: rollout plan for sentinel v1 -> v2 without breaking older controllers. Suggest feature-negotiation: controller declares supported sentinel_versions in handshake; runtime/prober uses highest supported.
Kai: Agreed. Use semantic minor versioning. v1.0 = current. v1.1 adds last_probe_ts. v2.0 would be breaking.
Maya: Can someone sketch the minimal JSON example we can use for docs?
Tom: Example: ```
{
  "version":"1.0",
  "health":"ok",
  "schema_hash":"9f2b1c",
  "kv_warmup_overall":86,
  "kv_warmup_worst_shard":70,
  "golden_match":"pass",
  "backpressure":"low",
  "last_probe_ts":"6219998870"
}
```
Aisha: Perfect. I'll put this into the RFC follow-up doc and open a tiny PR to add sentinel schema + tests. Thanks all. :sparkles:
